author: Bianca Caputo
title: Ice jam grows where Glen Creek flows into the Hudson - NewsBreak
text:
By Bianca Caputo ,
1 hours ago
JOHNSBURG, N.Y. ( NEWS10 ) — Under the Route 28 bridge in Johnsburg at the confluence of the Hudson River and Glen Creek, a large ice jam is partially blocking the channel.
Warren County Director of Public Affairs Don Lehman said in a phone interview that county crews, local fire departments and drones have been actively monitoring the situation. Lehman said the jam is currently stable.
Get the latest news, weather, sports and entertainment delivered right to your inbox! Lehman said jams can also trigger fast flooding and be unpredictable if ice completely blocks water flow, and that people nearby should have an emergency evacuation plan.
“There is a channel through there right now, which is good,” said Lehman. “…So the water is still moving.”
Download our WTEN+ streaming app on Roku, Fire TV and Apple TV! Lehman said that in any situation with an ice jam it’s important to maintain a safe distance, and take necessary precautions including monitoring water levels, keeping pets and children away and watching out for flood warnings.
“It’s not just the Hudson River problem,” said Lehman. “This is an issue that can happen really on any stream that has ice buildup.”
Montgomery County prepares for possible continued floods Local white water rafting river guide Ben Wallberg said he’s used to seeing these ice jams form, but the size is impressive.
“We bring trips down the Hudson River Gorge, which is a couple of miles up north from here,” said Wallberg.
Flood warning: Mohawk River ice jam causes road closures Another white water rafting guide and property owner in the area Brent Azaert said he’s seen people around the river stopping to get a look, and that he hopes people will be cautious.
“I’ve seen a lot of people walking down to take pictures of them,” said Azaert. “You never know when it’s going to start moving.”
SUNY Schenectady campus closed due to flooding Azaert built a cabin about 10 years ago on the edge of the river where he boils maple syrup in the spring. Now he says he’s just hoping for the best as the ice jam builds along the shore.
“It’s right down by the edge of the river, and it is currently surrounded by ice on all four sides,” said Azaert. “I’m thinking it’s not going to be in exactly the same spot that it was once the ice leaves.”
